note: Type Rush redesign (2026-10-14): a cleaner, minimal look in the style of TypingClub, still dark with the light blue accent. The phrase is much bigger and you type straight onto it (the text box is gone): typed letters turn light blue, mistakes turn red, the next letter is underlined, and a thin bar shows your progress. WPM, accuracy, progress and best WPM sit in four tidy cards at the top, and finished phrases are listed under the buttons. The finger guide was redrawn: a full keyboard with rounded keys (number row, Tab, Caps, Shift, Enter, Backspace, space bar) and two simple flat hands whose fingers rest on the home keys; the finger for the next key lights up in light blue and reaches the key while its hand leans toward it, with Shift and Backspace shown the same way. Wrapped lines no longer start with a space. Scoring, phrases, best WPM, the Weekly focus link and the Finger Guide on/off switch are unchanged; nothing was removed.

Car games 3D update (2026-10-14): F1 Cockpit: the steering wheel and the front tyres turned the opposite way to A / D and the touch arrows; they now turn the way you steer. The gearbox has ten gears instead of eight (same 115 mph top speed, closer gears), and the car and circuits have more blocky detail: a race number made of little blocks, nose camera pods, a multi-element front wing, bargeboards, a beam wing with a rain light, dials on the wheel and paddles that flick when you shift; braking boards before the bends, marshal posts with flags, TV camera towers, rubber laid down in the braking zones, a sponsor footbridge and an airship. Drift King is now 3D: night docks under sodium lamps with shipping containers, gantry cranes, a moored ship and the city across the water. Choose a Nissan Skyline GT-R (R34) or a 2021 Ford Mustang GT 5.0 and one of four courses, each harder than the last (Harbour Lot, Container Alley, Crane Yard, Pier Edge, where the sea is right beside you). Drifting builds a chain of points with a multiplier; blue clipping zones give a bonus; walls, spins and the sea cost points; medals and best scores are saved per car. Rally Race is now 3D and races like the F1 Cockpit, but off-road: choose a Subaru Impreza WRX STI or a Toyota GR Yaris Rally1 and one of four stages (Forest Gravel, Desert Canyon, Alpine Snow, Rainforest Mud, each harder than the last), then race two laps against three rival crews from the driver's seat or a chase camera. A co-driver calls the pace notes (bend direction and how tight, crests, jumps, water) with a countdown, spoken aloud when the browser has a voice; going off the road is rough and slippery and hitting trees or rocks damages the car. Take Your Time: every engine-assembly step now plays a fast-forward 3D clip of about ten seconds in a workshop, with a mechanic doing the job with the tools (rings fitted onto the piston with expander pliers and a compressor band, the piston tapped into the bore and the rod cap torqued on the crank, the head gasket, head, spiral bolt torque, camshaft, caps and timing chain, and the engine hoisted into the car); a missed timing check shows a fumble and the fix. The uphill and downhill stages are driven on a 3D mountain road against the AI. Scores, timing checks and points are unchanged. The previous 2D versions of Drift King, Rally and the Take Your Time pictures are kept and used automatically when WebGL is not available; nothing was removed.

Save chooser, User Saves and Infinite banner fix (2026-10-14): every save, export and back-up button now asks first what you want to save: the Block World, or User saves. The old Arcade Saves card is now called User Saves, and a User saves file holds everything except the Block World: your profile and picture, arcade progress and scores, badges and streak, coins, shop and themes, notes, flashcards and study data, AI memory and chat, My Files, the daily challenge, settings and saved keys, and your whole video library (included by default; with videos the file is a .wbsave, and you can untick them in the chooser). The Block World file holds the island and the Block World's own numbers only (rare-ore bank, best wave, Infinite day, most defenses built, graphics level). The chooser opens from Export progress, Back up (User / Saves tab and the 10-minute reminder bar) and the Save button inside Block World; Export world on the Block World card still saves the Block World straight away. Every Import button now recognises any file the app has ever saved (Block World, User saves, old Complete Save, old Full Backup, old progress files) and puts it in the right place; restoring User saves asks first, only touches this app's own items, never the Block World, and reloads the page. The in-game Load button now refuses a User saves file instead of wiping the island. Fixed: the day and night banner ('Night (calm), dawn in 40s' and the like) stayed on screen over every other tab and over the Block World mode picker; it now shows only while you are playing the Infinite world. Changed on request: the Block World Save button no longer writes the old Complete Save (arcade, AI and study data now live in User saves); old Complete Save files can still be loaded; nothing else was removed.

F1 Cockpit driving, crash and graphics update (2026-10-14): the cockpit is now a real 3D seat. You look out from the driver's eyes at the front tyres on their wishbones and pushrods, the halo, the steering wheel with a live screen and shift lights, your arms and two working rear-view mirrors that show the road behind, and there is no see-through floor any more. The body rolls in the bends, dives under braking, squats under power and shakes on the kerbs and gravel, and the wheels move on their suspension. The paint, the tarmac and the cockpit reflect the sky (High adds real bloom and light shafts), the ground has a blocky grass texture, and every circuit has floodlight towers. You now drive the car yourself: the gearbox is manual (Y shifts up, U shifts down, and the engine stays on the rev limiter until you shift), and the car has a real position across the road with grip, kerbs and gravel. Go too fast into a bend and it slides wide; keep steering one way and it leaves the road. Touching a barrier now disqualifies you, with one of twenty crash scenes picked at random (barrel roll, pole vault, inferno, cartwheel, pinball between the barriers, wheels off, tyre wall, split in two, T-bone and more). Each lasts about seven seconds with slow motion, TV-style camera cuts, sparks, smoke, fire, flying wheels and debris, a barrier that really breaks, and sound, and it scales with how hard you hit. A report then shows everything you had at that moment: the impact, the race, your tyres, the systems and your car. The corner prompt is only a warning now: the controls are at the top left, the map at the top right and a bright red countdown to the bend at the top, and missing a corner no longer ends the race. Fixed: on some circuits a building could stand on the track (buildings are now placed only where they fit), and the game ran faster on screens above 60 Hz (it now runs at the same speed everywhere). Touch screens got SHIFT UP and SHIFT DN buttons. The classic 2D cockpit is still used when WebGL is not available. Changed on request: the automatic gear change and the rule that ended the race on a missed corner prompt were replaced by the manual gearbox and the warning; nothing else was removed.

F1 Cockpit 3D update (2026-10-14): the live feed is now a real 3D scene instead of a painted flat road. The circuit is built from the same track points the minimap and the TURN LEFT / TURN RIGHT prompts use, so every bend, kerb and wall matches the game, and the ground rolls with hills, with a bridge where the figure-eight crosses itself. Trees, hills and clouds are blocky in the Block World style (square trunks and stacked boxes, nothing round), and the track has grandstands (with crowds on High), a pit building, sponsor boards with made-up names, a start gantry with lights, a start grid, tyre walls and catch fences. Rival cars are now real 3D cars with spinning wheels that you pass on the road, and the sun casts shadows. Every circuit has its own time of day: Midday, Golden hour, Cool morning and Sunset. A light shader pass adds speed blur, vignette, colour grading and tone mapping. New Graphics button next to Restart cycles Low, Balanced and High and remembers your choice; it starts on Balanced, or on Low the first time on a Chromebook or other slow-looking machine. The cockpit, steering wheel, minimap, telemetry and corner prompts are unchanged and still driven by the same game state. If WebGL is not available, or is lost during a race, the previous 2D feed is used automatically. The figure-eight now starts on a straight instead of under its bridge, and the very tight notches of the Complex and Curvy circuits are eased slightly in 3D so the road does not fold over itself. Fix: closing the cockpit now stops its loop, sound and keys (before, W / A / S / D / Y / U / P / T stayed captured by the page after closing it). Nothing was removed.

F1 Cockpit depth and sun update (2026-10-13): the sun now has a real position in the world, so it swings across the sky as the car turns round the track (the sky, hills, trees and grandstands now rotate with the road instead of sliding a few pixels), and it lights the cockpit from its angle: rim light and shadow sides on the halo, tyres, nose, wheel and bodywork, a shadow of the halo strut on the nose, glare on the screen, mirrors and road, a warm haze and lens flare when you drive toward it, and rival car shadows that fall away from it. The halo is now a shaded, tapered 3D tube. Your head now moves with the cornering G-force: in a right turn the view moves left, in a left turn it moves right, and near parts (wheel, halo) shift more than far parts (nose, tyres, front wing, world), so everything has parallax. Nothing was removed.

F1 Cockpit road now follows the real track (2026-10-13): the road in the live feed used to bend from a made-up wave, so it could curve right while the prompt and map said left. It is now projected from the actual track points (the same ones the minimap and the TURN LEFT / TURN RIGHT prompts use), so left turns bend the road left and right turns bend it right, starting from the point you are at on the lap. Each turn prompt now sits on a real corner (nudged up to six points from its old slot) so its direction agrees with the map marker and the road bend. The sky and hills pan with the bend. Nothing was removed.

F1 Cockpit fix and slim-down (2026-10-12): your car is now complete, with a front wing, bodywork and a full nose cone, and the halo arms land on the cockpit rim. Rival cars were rebuilt: they now move at the same pace scale as you (before they circled the track about three times faster than you could ever drive), start on the grid just ahead of you, shrink with true perspective, run in lanes beside your nose and tyres so none are half hidden, and slide past your side when you overtake. To lighten the game, the old unused cockpit and rival drawing code was deleted (authorized), and the sky, hills, trees and vignette are drawn once and reused instead of every frame; the glow effects now use cheap overlays. Graphics are otherwise the same.

F1 Cockpit realism update (2026-10-12): the live feed now has a scrolling daylight track with red/white kerbs, gravel, walls and ad boards, sky with sun and clouds, hills, trees, grandstand and pit building, camera shake, speed streaks and a vignette. Rival cars are redrawn with shaded bodies, tyres, rear wings and rain lights, drift laterally, and now pass by your side window when you overtake them. The cockpit was redrawn from real F1 references: halo with centre strut, carbon weave, front tyres with Pirelli band and wishbones, mirrors, nose cone, and a full steering wheel with rev LEDs, LCD, coloured buttons, rotary dials and gloved hands. The old renderers are kept as an automatic fallback. Nothing was removed.

Infinite defenses finished and fixed (2026-10-11): House, Farm, Mine, Workshop, Market and Armory work again (an older script outside the game was catching the clicks and then failing); they now use the same green/red placement preview as defenses, and Workshop, Market and Armory open their menus when you click the placed building. The Watch Tower is a real timber tower on a stone base with a ladder, a roofed lookout, a flag and a lantern, and a helper stands in it while it is manned. Torches now give off light at night: a flickering flame, a halo, a glow on the ground and real light on nearby blocks. Walls are real oriented blocks that you can turn (R, Shift+R, [ and ]), and they snap onto towers and onto each other so a line of walls can join up (Snap button to turn this off). When your castle falls or the king dies a defeat screen shows your run: day and waves survived, zombies killed, damage dealt and taken, wood and iron gained, helpers, troops, siege weapons, buildings and defenses built, with Play again and Main menu buttons. Fixed a shaded box on wide screens: the screen vignette was capped at 1280 pixels wide and now covers the whole view.

Block World visuals and siege effects (2026-10-10): sky grade with a golden sun, warm dawn and dusk horizon, moonlit nights and a blood sky on zombie nights; bump-mapped blocks with a pixel grain; sun glow and drifting ambient motes (pollen by day, fireflies at night, embers on blood nights); rock explosions, catapult and crossbow effects with recoil and small camera shake. (Logged late: this entry was missing when 5.58.0 was made.)

Performance monitor and Assistant memory lock (2026-10-10): Developer options has a new Performance monitor section. Switch it on and a small FPS / frame time / memory / game speed readout shows on every page. With Auto quality on, it lowers game quality one step at a time when the device struggles (Full, then Reduced, which turns Shaders off and stops decorative background animation, then Lite, which also draws Block World at lower resolution) and puts quality back slowly once things run smoothly, which helps at 10x speed on a Chromebook; turning the monitor off restores Full. Manual quality buttons are there too. The Assistant memory is now locked: adding, deleting, clearing, importing or restoring a memory (from the Developer tab, the Assistant page, the Save this exchange buttons, or a complete save) opens a code prompt first, and nothing changes unless the correct code is typed by a person. Wrong codes change nothing and five wrong tries pause the prompt for 15 seconds. This is a client-side lock like the other gates, not a security boundary. Also fixed: the Assistant page memory card could not see the memory at all (its list stayed empty and Save memory did nothing), and complete saves skipped the memory; both now work.

Infinite boss nights, defenses with crews, weather and blood moons (2026-10-10): every 10th wave (Day 19, 29 and so on) a boss zombie arrives with its own health bar at the top of the screen; beat it before dawn for coins or rare Gold and Diamond blocks (a Claim button appears in the Classic world to put them in your hotbar, which now has Gold and Diamond slots on keys 6 and 7). Defenses are rebuilt inside the game: Wall, Tower, Torch and Demolish plus a new Trap (20 wood, six spike hits, slows and hurts zombies); your helper soldiers now man towers at night (towers fire twice as fast and hit harder) and repair damaged walls, towers and traps, refilling traps, and go back to gathering wood when there is nothing to do. Weather: each Infinite day is clear, rainy or foggy; rain slows zombies and draws rain, fog shortens how far you can see and hides far zombies and weakens tower range. Some nights from wave 3 are a blood moon (red moon and sky, announced that morning) with twice as many zombies. Nothing was removed; the old Wall, Tower, Torch and Demolish buttons are hidden because the new ones replace them.

Watch Later, history and a Block World clip recorder (2026-10-10): Media > Video > Online now has Search, Watch later and History buttons. Tap the clock on any video (or the Watch later button while it plays) to save it, then replay it in one tap without searching again; everything you play is also kept in History (the last 60). Block World (both modes) has a new Record clip button in the top-left corner: press it to start, press again to stop, and the clip is saved straight into Media > Video > Library where you can play it back (it stops by itself after 5 minutes or if you leave Block World; if the browser storage is full the clip is downloaded instead). Nothing was removed.

Online video now actually plays (2026-10-10): YouTube refuses its embedded player on pages opened as a local file (error 153), so the Online page now plays videos as a plain video file streamed through a public server, which works from a local file; it tries several servers at once and moves on if one fails, and a quality picker appears when more than one size is offered (usually 360p, sometimes 720p). Switch player cycles direct stream, YouTube embed and alternate embed (the YouTube embed is used first when Workbench is opened from an http/https address, and the app switches to the direct stream by itself on error 153). The server list also refreshes from the Invidious directory when online. Nothing was removed.

Infinite 10x speed and online YouTube-style video (2026-10-09): Infinite mode now has a 10x speed button next to the 2x button (pressing one switches the other off; both only show in Infinite and reset to 1x when you leave; if the device cannot keep up, 10x eases off instead of freezing). Media > Video has a new Online page, now the first and default page: it checks that you are connected to Wi-Fi, lets you search YouTube or paste a link, and plays videos straight from YouTube over the internet (nothing is downloaded). Search uses your own YouTube Data API key (saved in this browser only) or, without a key, free public search servers that are sometimes down. If YouTube refuses to embed a video, Open on YouTube and Try alternate player are one tap away. Library, Sync and Share are unchanged. Nothing was removed.

Infinite 2x fix, scrolling and AI access-code rule (2026-10-08): the Infinite mode 2x speed button was missing because its code loaded before the game and could not see it; it now lives inside the game, shows next to the build buttons only in Infinite, and resets to 1x when you leave. Every page (tab) now scrolls when its content is taller than the screen (the Block World play screen keeps its own touch controls and is the only one that does not scroll, and arcade pop-up screens now scroll too). New AI Access Code Rule in Developer Options (Rules list and AI Memory System): no AI may edit anything or do anything unless the user has entered the access code first. Nothing was removed.

Assistant files and summary, weekly focus, badges (2026-10-08): Assistant My files - drop .txt or .md files into the Local Memory card and the best matching passages are added to your questions automatically (kept under about 15 percent of the model context, source file and part shown under the reply, all stored in this browser, also used by the memory-only brain). Assistant auto-summary - when a chat passes about 75 percent of the context the older messages are condensed into a pinned summary at the top of the chat (kept in the prompt, shrinks itself if it grows, Forget summary button) instead of being dropped. Weekly focus on Start - wrong answers from flashcards, the notes quiz, Spanish, Algebra and Type Rush are collected for 7 days into one list with one-tap practice; two right answers in a row clear an item. Badges on User / Saves - 20 cross-area badges (Day 10 survivor, 7-day streak, deck builder, Fixer-Upper and more) that pay coins into the shop balance, with a daily-visit streak counter and unlock toasts. Rule checker now tracks the new panels.

Infinite 2x speed, wave report card, F1 tyres and corner coach (2026-10-08): Infinite mode has a 2x speed button (only shown in Infinite, resets when you leave); after every night a report card shows zombies defeated, walls lost, castle health, the dawn bonus, coins earned (2 plus 2 per wave, up to 25) and your best wave, which is saved. F1 now has three tyre compounds (Soft grips most but wears fastest, Medium, Hard) with a live wear readout, a T key to choose the next set and a P key to pit at the next start/finish line (a 2.6 second stop that fits fresh tyres), plus PIT and TYRE buttons on touch screens. After every lap a corner coach shows how long you waited after each warning (green, yellow or red), flags missed corners and compares you with your last 5 laps, saved on this device. Nothing was removed.

Block World defenses and phone controls (2026-10-08): Infinite mode gains Wall (15 wood, zombies cannot walk through and chew it down), Tower (60 wood, shoots the nearest zombie) and Torch (10 wood, slows zombies nearby), all placed with the green/red preview; a Demolish mode removes your own buildings and defenses for a 50% wood refund; press R (or the rotate button) to turn a building while placing. On touch screens Block World now has an on-screen move stick, turn and zoom buttons, and placement is drag to aim then tap Place, Rotate or Cancel. F1 already had on-screen controls and is unchanged. Defenses are not saved with the world yet. Nothing was removed.

Developer layout and smoke test (2026-10-08): added a second checker under the rule checker in Developer Options. It finds Block World buttons and HUD pieces that overlap or sit off screen (open Classic or Infinite first, it tests the screen size you are on), duplicate element ids, errors the page has logged since it loaded, tab buttons that point at missing panels, and how much browser storage is used. The new checker is also on the tracked-feature list. Nothing was removed.

Block World layout fix (2026-10-08): the Day/night/zombie timer banner no longer stays on screen after you leave Block World (it was only hidden by the game loop, which stops on other tabs); the Block World buttons in Classic and Infinite are now stacked in two tidy columns (left: mode, status, save/load; right: performance, shader, rain, follow king, Instructions) so none sit on top of each other, and the build row and stats wrap instead of overlapping on narrow phone screens. Nothing was removed.

F1 Cockpit update (2026-10-07): the car now has 8 forward gears like a modern F1 car (was 6), with the speed bands, rev display and shifting spread across all 8; the corner warning time now scales with speed (2 seconds at 50 mph or less, 4 seconds at 100 mph or more, smoothly in between) instead of a fixed 3 seconds; and the generic buzzing engine tone was replaced by a layered, saturated and filtered high-revving V10-style sound. Nothing was removed.

Block World update (2026-10-07): the Stone currency was replaced by Iron everywhere in Legacy and Infinite (HUD, mines, markets, docks, ships; the Stone block material and terrain are unchanged); the always-on instruction text is now behind an Instructions button that opens a pop-up; and buildings are placed by you: choose House, Farm, Mine, Workshop, Market or Armory, hover anywhere to see a see-through copy of that building (green = free, red = blocked by a building, farm, castle, ore, water or the territory edge), and click to place only on green (right-click or Esc cancels). Workshops now actually get built, and clicking one opens its production menu. Docks and bridges still pick their own spot. Nothing else was removed.

Assistant lock fix and rule checker upgrade (2026-10-07): fixed the Assistant lock page staying on screen after a correct access code. Two CSS rules forced the lock page to display with higher priority than the rule that hides it once unlocked, so the hide rule now matches the same selector strength. The Developer rule checker (added in 5.46.0, checked and still present) gained a check that the Assistant lock page actually hides when unlocked. Nothing was removed.

Infinite world rework (2026-10-07): Infinite now builds one island in the middle of the sea (grass, then a ring of sand, then water; no rocks, cliffs or ore) with only your castle and no other kingdoms. It shares Legacy mechanics (building, resources, units, day/night) but not its AI-kingdom gameplay, so there is no victory screen. Zombies start on the night of Day 10 and each day brings more of them (5, then +3 per day, up to 100); they leave small fading blood-drip footprints as they walk. The top banner shows the time to night and the wave. Nothing was removed.

Infinite world update (2026-10-07): Infinite > Enter World now runs on the Legacy engine, so it looks and plays like Legacy (terrain, HUD, building, kingdoms, units, and every Legacy update) with your castle and king in the middle of the map. From the night of Day 10, a zombie wave attacks every night (bigger each night); a banner at the top shows the time until night and the current wave, and surviving until dawn pays wood. Load Save File still opens the classic free-build sandbox. Nothing was removed.

Tools update (2026-10-07): added the Developer rule checker (badge/APP_VERSION, changelog entry, filename, patch rollover, tracked features present, changelog not shortened); a Back up everything / Restore button in User / Saves with a reminder every 10 minutes; and a Coin shop with three new themes and three accent colors bought with arcade coins. Fixed a bug from 5.44.0/5.45.0 where the Assistant Save-as-Project-Rule button and the /help, /note and empty /summarize commands could not reach the Assistant code (added window.wbBridge). Nothing was removed.

Assistant and Arcade update (2026-10-07): added Assistant slash commands (/quiz, /explain, /summarize expand into full prompts; /note saves to Study Notes; /help lists them), and an Arcade daily challenge: one rotating game per day with today's best score, a day streak, a recent-days leaderboard stored locally, and a DAILY tag with best and streak on that game's cabinet tile. Nothing was removed.

Study and Assistant update (2026-10-07): added spaced-repetition flashcard review (missed cards return in 10 minutes, known cards are pushed days out) with a due-today count on the Start tab; added a fill-in-the-blank quiz built from Study Notes whose wrong answers are added to the flashcards; and the Assistant now shows which saved memories each reply used and offers to save the exchange as a Project Rule or Study Note. Nothing was removed.

Lock screens and Developer background (2026-10-06): the Assistant lock now matches the Developer options lock (a card inside the page with the navigation still visible, covering the whole content area edge to edge). Both lock cards have a blue glow that dims up and down, and much bigger titles in the style of Welcome Developer (the Developer lock title now uses the same Dev accent word). The Developer background squares now drift diagonally from top left to bottom right and glow with a slow breathing pulse; the Assistant lock uses the same moving grid. Reduced-motion settings still turn the animation off. The Back to Start button on the Assistant lock is hidden because the navigation is visible again; nothing was removed from the code.

Layout patch (2026-10-06): the Start tab now scrolls (its container was sized to its full content and clipped, so it could never scroll; it now fills the window and scrolls inside it). The Assistant lock screen now covers the entire window edge to edge (a generic tab-content width limit was shrinking it and leaving the left and right sides uncovered), has a dimmed blurred backdrop, and gained a Back to Start button so the navigation stays reachable. Page content on every tab, including Data and Developer Options, is now centered in the middle of the window instead of hugging one side. No existing features, data, or code were removed.

F1 cockpit detail overhaul (2026-10-05): redrew the first-person cockpit with a carbon-fibre weave, halo and centre strut, nose cone and front wing, front tyres with suspension arms, wing mirrors and carbon side cowls. Rival cars are now detailed rear views with rear wing and endplates, DRS slot, rain light, halo, helmet, airbox, diffuser and rear tyres. The steering wheel is now a real F1-style wheel (display, LED rev lights, buttons, rotaries, gloved grips) and it turns with steering input in both the cockpit view and the HUD wheel. All telemetry and controls are unchanged.

Detailed cover art (2026-10-05): redrew every Arcade cover with much more detail. Each cover now has a lit background with an accent-color glow, a soft bevel and drop shadow so shapes look raised, a vignette, a gloss highlight, and film grain, plus game-specific scene detail such as lit windows and motion lines in Rooftop Rumble, ripples, bubbles and reeds in Fishing Hole, crystal facets, sparkles and light rays in Crystal Garden, a floor grid and beam glow in Laser Dodge, and kerbs and a racing line in Apex Hunter.

Arcade cover art (2026-10-05): every cabinet in the Arcade library now has its own illustrated cover that shows what the game is about, for example a rooftop duel for Rooftop Rumble, a lit pit-lane tire for Pit Stop Pro, a laser-cut room for Laser Dodge, and a raked sand circle for Zen Garden. Covers are drawn as scalable vector art in each category color, show larger on the game tiles and the detail panel, and fall back to the old icon if a cover is ever missing.

Start page notice, animated background and richer game descriptions (2026-10-05): added a notice above the Tutorial card stating that Workbench is a tool made for studying and for people without internet access, is not a game or an AI, and must not be shared (versioning and tracking are used to enforce this). Replaced the Start background with glowing blue lines that wander across a dev-tools-style grid, light up the squares they pass through, leave a long fading trail, and pulse in brightness. Rewrote the Arcade descriptions for 66 games into fuller, store-page-style summaries shown in the library detail panel.

Layout fixes and versioning rule (2026-10-05): the Start page is now centered, and the F1 Cockpit window is wider with a re-flowed layout so the steering wheel and panels are no longer cut off. Version numbering now rolls every 10 patches into a minor update (5.40.9 + 1 = 5.41.0), and this release is 5.41.0 + 1 more patch for the 5.40.x changes; the rule is saved in Developer Options under AI Memory System.

Arcade library remake (2026-10-04): the Games view is now a Steam-style library. A left list holds Library, All games, Favorites, Recently played, the Patience, Fast, and Skill collections, and Coming soon. The middle shows cover-style tiles on horizontal shelves, with a circling bright-blue ring on the selected tile. A details panel shows the description, best score, difficulty, a Play button, and a favorite toggle, becoming a bottom sheet on phones. Search, difficulty, favorites, scores, and recents all use the existing profile data, and Play now also records Recently played. The original cabinet code is kept intact but hidden, the car guys and Block World tabs are unchanged, and Arcade cyan is now the classic bright blue (#1fb6ff). The Arcade tour steps were updated to match.

Welcome tour rewrite (2026-10-04): the first-visit tour is now a friendly ten-step walkthrough with a titled card, a plain-language description of each area, and a Try it tip showing how to interact. It covers Start, the tab bar, Start cards, Educational, Type Rush, Media, Arcade (including its filters, difficulty, and favorites), and User / Saves. The Assistant and Developer options tabs are intentionally left out of the tour because they are for the owner. The old fixed seven-tab caption was removed, the final button now reads Let’s go, and the Take the tour replay button is unchanged.

Type Rush finger guide realism (2026-10-04): replaced the thin claw-like fingers with proper hands: thicker, shorter, rounded fingers with knuckles, a palm, a thumb, and a wrist and forearm that fade out below. When the next key is far from the home row, the whole hand now slides and turns at the wrist while the active finger reaches onto the glowing key, and the other fingers follow the hand like a real typist. The resting hands, line-art style, on/off toggle, Shift and Backspace hints, and all telemetry are unchanged.

Type Rush finger guide restyle (2026-10-04): the guide now draws quiet line-art hands resting on the home row of a simpler keyboard, in the style of TypingClub. The active finger outlines in bright blue and reaches onto the glowing target key, thumbs handle the space bar, and everything else stays dim so it is not overwhelming. Removed the rainbow finger colors, number row, and dashed pointer line. The Finger Guide toggle, Shift and Backspace hints, and all telemetry are unchanged.

Type Rush redesign (2026-10-04): black background with light-grey phrase letters, every former cyan or mint accent is now bright blue, and the Type Rush title is bright blue with a ring circling the whole title like the Educational cabinets. Added an optional Finger Guide under the phrase that shows an on-screen keyboard and both hands, highlights the next key and the finger to use (including Shift and Backspace), and can be switched on or off from the button row with the choice remembered. Arcade cabinet #1 built: "Rooftop Rumble", a 2D fighting game with articulated (torso/hips/shoulders/elbows) fighters, drawn on canvas — 2-player local, or vs. CPU (easy/hard). Cabinet loads lazily on tap, opens fullscreen, and unloads back to an idle tile when closed. Grid has 3 more open "next cabinet" slots for future games.

Rooftop Rumble fighters got a detail pass: face (brow, eye highlight, nose, mouth, ear, bandana tail), pec/ab shading, a belt with buckle, stitched vest trim, muscle highlights on upper arms/thighs, kneepads, wrist wraps, real gloved fists with knuckle creases, and shoes with soles + laces.

Fighters now breathe and sweat. A fatigue value builds from throwing/landing hits and rises as HP drops, driving: visible chest rise/fall (shoulders shift with each breath, faster and deeper when winded), an open panting mouth with a puff of visible breath on hard exhales, glossy sweat sheen and sliding beads on the forehead/temple and upper arms once fatigue passes a threshold, and a flicked sweat droplet (with real gravity) on every clean unblocked hit.

Walk cycle rebuilt to read as a step instead of a scissoring sprite: knee flexion is now phase-shifted from hip swing, arms carry a matching elbow bend, and a twice-per-stride vertical bob plus side-to-side hip sway were added (shadow stays ground-anchored while the body shifts above it). The bandana tail and a new hanging belt sash are both real hinged cloth now — a light damped pendulum driven by velocity and torso lean swings them behind the fighter’s motion instead of holding one fixed drawn shape. Added a subtle procedural skin-grain texture (pores/creases) across the head, torso, and bare limbs.

Rooftop Rumble now keeps a win/loss/draw record with a KO-to-win ratio (KOs vs. clock-outs), shown on the Arcade tab and the mode-select screen. Closing the cabinet offers to export that record to a small .json file. New "Log in" tab (between Arcade and Developer options) re-imports that file to restore your record and display name, here or on another device, with a one-click reset back to a fresh Guest profile.

Replaced the export-on-close popup and the "Log in" tab with one "Update / Export / Import" tab (same spot, between Arcade and Developer options). It holds two separate cards — Block World and Arcade — each with its own export/import file, so loading one never touches the other. World export/import here calls the exact same save functions as the canvas-corner Save/Load buttons, which still work too.

Rooftop Rumble fighters reworked for a gritty, Mortal Kombat-style realism pass: detailed face (iris/pupil/highlight eye, eyebrow, nose bridge + nostril, lips/teeth, cheekbone shading, jawline, facial stubble), defined musculature (deltoid caps, separate pec bellies with cleavage, 6-pack abs with linea alba, oblique striations, biceps peak, quadriceps separation, calf bulge, visible forearm veins when fatigued), progressive damage system (rib bruising, under-eye bruising, blood drips on face, torn vest at high damage, accumulating blood decals on torso, blood pool on ground), blood splatter particles on every hit, darker grittier skin tones, darker atmospheric arena with stronger vignette and no window flicker.

Arcade cabinet #2 built: "Neon Sprint", a top-down arcade racer with a procedurally curving road, traffic to dodge, roadside scenery (trees, lamp posts), detailed car rendering (body gradient, windshield, headlights/taillights, wheels, driver), speed/distance/time HUD, 3 crash lives, and win/loss record tracking. Profile system updated to track both cabinets. Three difficulty modes: Time Trial, Traffic Dodge, and Hard Traffic.

Neon Sprint: added Infinite mode — endless road with no time limit, moderate traffic, reach 5000m to win or crash 3 times to lose. Win/loss results tracked in profile and compatible with import/export.

Supports multiple videos, chunked transfer with progress indicators.

Mobile responsiveness improvements.

Win condition changed: must destroy all enemy castles, not just kill soldiers.
